pageCache.pageTitle: Clayesmore Vision and Values | Every Child Known & Valued
pageCache.text:
Vision & Values
Right School for Your Child?
Some children are capable but lack confidence. Some work hard yet go unnoticed in busy classrooms. Some need time, encouragement, and teachers who truly see them. Clayesmore is a school where every child is embraced, understood, and empowered to flourish. If your child would thrive in a place that celebrates individuality, nurtures talent, and encourages growth in every form, Clayesmore could be the right school for your family.
Our Purpose
Clayesmore has always educated children by knowing them well. Teaching happens in small groups, with teachers deeply involved in the wider life of the school, taking personal responsibility for each child’s learning. We take the time to understand how pupils work best and create opportunities for them to grow academically, socially, and personally.
Our distinctive LEX programme, spanning Prep to Sixth Form, provides structured experiences that develop character, leadership, resilience, and confidence. Pupils are encouraged to try new things, take responsibility, work with others, and discover their potential in a supportive environment.
Our Promise
At Clayesmore, every child is known, noticed, and respected. Pastoral care is part of everyone’s role, not just a few specialists. Progress is monitored closely, concerns are picked up early, and effort is celebrated as much as achievement. We value children not just for what they accomplish but for who they are becoming. Within our strong, inclusive community, pupils learn to persevere, be kind, and exceed their own expectations—growing into thoughtful, articulate, and confident young adults.
If you are looking for a school where your child is genuinely seen, encouraged, and challenged; where ambition is nurtured alongside compassion; and where personal growth matters as much as academic success, Clayesmore is a place where your child can belong, thrive, and quietly discover the magic of who they can become.

pageCache.pageTitle: Clayesmore Nursery Head's Welcome | Hannah Miles, Dorset
pageCache.text:
Nursery Head’s Welcome
It is a true privilege not only to lead an early years setting, but to have the opportunity to create it from the very beginning. It feels especially meaningful as I spent part of my own childhood growing up in this wonderful village and community that has always held a special place in my heart.
With more than 20 years of experience in early years education, a degree in Childhood Studies and specialist early years qualifications, I am passionate about giving every child the very best start in life. I believe childhood should be filled with wonder, curiosity, kindness and a strong sense of belonging.
At Clayesmore Nursery, every decision has been carefully considered to create an environment where children feel safe, valued and inspired to learn. Our beautiful nursery has been thoughtfully designed to provide calm, nurturing spaces, natural resources and endless opportunities for exploration, creativity and outdoor adventure.
Relationships are at the heart of everything we do. By working closely with families, we create a genuine partnership that supports every child’s unique journey. We celebrate each milestone, nurture confidence and independence, and encourage children to develop a lifelong love of learning through meaningful play and memorable experiences.
My vision is not simply to provide exceptional care and education today, but to create a nursery that leaves a lasting legacy for generations of children and families to come.
As Winnie the Pooh so beautifully said: “We didn’t realise we were making memories, we just knew we were having fun.” Those words perfectly capture what childhood should be.
Hannah Miles Head of Nursery
It is an honour to be part of the Clayesmore community, and I very much look forward to welcoming your family to Clayesmore Nursery as we begin this exciting new chapter together.

pageCache.pageTitle: Clayesmore Head’s Welcome | Inclusive Excellence in Dorset
pageCache.text:
Head’s Welcome
A warm welcome
There is a quality that is easier to feel than it is to describe that strikes a family on their first visit to Clayesmore. The campus is impressive, the facilities are excellent, but it is the atmosphere that stays with you: ambitious, warm, and genuinely alive.
Clayesmore was founded on the belief that education should be about the whole child and that conviction has never left us. We call it ‘Inclusive Excellence’ and it is at the heart of everything we do: aspiration and care are not in tension here, they are the same thing. Every pupil is known and supported and, with excellence and ambition at our core, every pupil is challenged to reach beyond what they thought possible.
We are one of the few schools in the country that offers a complete journey from Nursery all the way through to Sixth Form, for day pupils and boarders alike. That continuity gives children something valuable: the confidence that comes from being truly known over many years. Each stage feels distinct but remains part of the whole and our 62 acres of North Dorset countryside give that journey a setting unlike almost anywhere else.
In the classroom, on the sports field, in the boarding house and on the stage we ensure that every pupil finds their version of excellence. They leave us knowing who they are, well-prepared for life beyond the school gates and with confidence and character. Whether they head off to Oxbridge, a university in the UK or abroad, to an apprenticeship, the military, the world of business or to inherit the family farm, they have the qualifications, habits and aptitudes needed to thrive in the modern world.
Individualised teaching and learning, high quality pastoral care, a rich co-curricular life and fantastic facilities combine to form a unique experience. Central to all of this is our LEX programme. Delivered on Saturday mornings over five years, it builds the skills, confidence and self-knowledge that no timetable of lessons alone can provide. It is distinctive, it is ours, and the pupils love it.
Choosing a school is a significant decision, and the fit matters more than any ranking. I would encourage you to come and see us, to walk around the campus, meet the staff, and spend time with the pupils. That visit will tell you everything a brochure cannot.
I very much look forward to welcoming you.

pageCache.pageTitle: History of Clayesmore School | Heritage in Dorset Since 1933
pageCache.text:
History
A History of Clayesmore
Clayesmore’s story began in 1896, long before the school found its permanent home in the Dorset countryside. Founded by Alexander “Lex” Devine, an educational pioneer with a progressive approach to education, Clayesmore was built around the belief that every pupil should be encouraged to think independently, develop their character and discover their own strengths.
1896 – The beginning in Enfield
Clayesmore was founded in 1896 in Enfield, Middlesex, by Alexander “Lex” Devine. At a time when education was often rooted in tradition and conformity, Devine had a different vision. He believed in educating the whole person and giving young people the confidence to think for themselves.
His philosophy was captured in the school motto, “Think of yourself” – an invitation not to be self-centred, but to develop independent thought, judgement and responsibility.
That principle remains relevant to Clayesmore today. The belief that every child is different, with their own talents, interests and ambitions, has been part of the school’s character from the very beginning.
1902 – Pangbourne
As the school grew, Clayesmore moved west to Pangbourne in Berkshire in 1902. It was the second home in the school’s early history, as Devine continued to develop his distinctive approach to education.
1914 – Northwood Park
In 1914, Clayesmore moved once again, this time to Northwood Park in Hampshire, where it remained for almost two decades.
These early years were an important part of Clayesmore’s development. The school may have changed its surroundings, but its founding principles remained constant: independence, character, curiosity and an appreciation that education should extend beyond the classroom.
1933 – A new home in Dorset
In 1933, Clayesmore moved to Iwerne Minster in Dorset, where it has remained ever since.
The school acquired a remarkable Victorian estate centred around an impressive mansion designed by the celebrated Gothic Revival architect Alfred Waterhouse, best known for London’s Natural History Museum. Completed in 1878, the house was originally built as a private residence for George Glyn, 2nd Baron Wolverton.
The house had already enjoyed a fascinating history before Clayesmore arrived. One of its notable owners was James Ismay, son of Thomas Henry Ismay, founder of the White Star Line. When the Ismay family moved to the house, they brought elements of their previous home with them. Among them was the extraordinary fireplace in the main reception room, which was transported brick by brick from their former mansion at Dawpool. It remains a striking feature of the house today.
A school shaped by its surroundings
When Lex Devine brought Clayesmore to Iwerne Minster, the school found a setting in which its educational philosophy could flourish. Over time, the historic house became the heart of a growing school, surrounded by 62 acres of Dorset countryside.
Today, the estate includes sports pitches, woodland, gardens and a picturesque lake, which has become an enduring part of school life. The lake and its surrounding landscape provide opportunities for outdoor learning as well as recreation, from Prep pupils exploring the natural environment to the famous cross-country relays that take runners around the estate.
The grounds are not simply a backdrop to school life. They are part of the experience of being at Clayesmore, providing space to learn, explore, compete, create and spend time together.
130 years of Clayesmore
Over the decades, Clayesmore has continued to evolve. From its beginnings as a small school founded by Lex Devine, it has grown into an all-through school educating children from Nursery through to Sixth Form, while retaining the sense of individuality that has been central to its identity since 1896.
The school has continued to combine its heritage with new ideas, modern facilities and an increasingly broad academic and co-curricular offering. Yet the principle at its heart remains remarkably consistent: there is no single path through education, and every pupil should be encouraged to discover and shape their own.
Today, Clayesmore is proud of both parts of its story – its progressive beginnings and its remarkable Dorset home. The Victorian Main House, the surrounding landscape and the traditions built over generations all form part of the school’s character, while the pupils themselves continue to shape its future.

pageCache.pageTitle: Performing Arts | Beyond the Classroom at Clayesmore
pageCache.text:
Performing Arts at Clayesmore
The Prep and Senior Performing Arts departments at Clayesmore are vibrant, ambitious and exciting, providing pupils with an exceptional range of opportunities to perform, create, collaborate and develop confidence through the performing arts.
At the heart of our programme is our designated professional theatre, situated on the Clayesmore grounds. This provides pupils with an authentic theatre experience and allows them to develop an understanding of what it is like to work within a professional performing arts environment.
A Professional Theatre Experience
Our theatre is much more than simply a space in which pupils perform. It provides a professional environment with stage lighting, professional sound equipment, media and projection facilities, backstage areas and technical support. Pupils have the opportunity to experience many of the different roles involved in bringing a production to life, both on and off stage.
A professional theatre environment involves an enormous amount of teamwork. Alongside the performers are directors, musical directors, choreographers, lighting technicians, sound technicians, stage managers, costume and make-up teams, backstage crew and front-of-house staff. Our pupils are therefore encouraged to understand that a successful production is created through the contribution of an entire team.
Working in this environment enables pupils to develop valuable skills in communication, leadership, organisation, resilience, creativity, teamwork and problem-solving, while also gaining confidence in front of an audience.
The theatre also gives pupils the opportunity to experience the excitement of technical rehearsals, dress rehearsals, lighting states, sound checks, microphones, stage entrances, scene changes and live performance. For many pupils, performing on a professional-style stage in front of a large audience is an incredibly memorable and formative experience.
The Prep School has a strong tradition of ambitious and colourful musical productions, involving pupils across the school and giving children the opportunity to perform in a professional theatre environment.
One of our recent major productions was Joseph and the Amazing Technicolor Dreamcoat, performed by pupils in Years 6–8.
This was a particularly vibrant and energetic production, with a cast of approximately 50 pupils. The production brought together singing, acting, choreography, costume, staging, lighting and sound to create a spectacular theatrical experience.
The colourful nature of Joseph provided pupils with the opportunity to explore a wide range of musical and theatrical styles, from the energetic opening numbers through to the more dramatic and emotional moments of the story. The production was filled with bold colour, imaginative costumes, ensemble singing, choreography and lively staging, creating a visually exciting experience for both performers and audiences.
Pupils developed their skills through an extended rehearsal process in LEX, learning individual musical parts while also understanding the importance of working as an ensemble. They had to listen carefully to one another, respond to musical direction, learn choreography, remember stage positions and develop confidence in delivering their characters.
The production culminated in performances to large, enthusiastic audiences, giving pupils the enormous satisfaction of seeing their months of preparation come together on stage.
For many of our younger performers, this is their first experience of taking part in a large-scale musical theatre production, and it provides an invaluable introduction to the discipline, commitment and excitement of live performance.
The Senior School’s performing arts programme provides pupils with opportunities to take on increasingly challenging and sophisticated theatrical work.
The Senior School recently staged Sweeney Todd: The Demon Barber of Fleet Street, involving pupils from Years 9–13.
This was a significantly more mature and demanding production, allowing our older pupils to explore dark musical theatre, characterisation, dramatic storytelling and complex musical material.
Sweeney Todd, with music and lyrics by Stephen Sondheim, is a dramatic musical centred around the barber Sweeney Todd and his return to Victorian London seeking revenge. The production explores themes of revenge, justice, obsession, ambition and morality, and its distinctive musical score presents considerable challenges for young performers.
The production required pupils to develop sophisticated acting skills alongside demanding vocal and musical abilities. Characters needed to be carefully developed, with performers exploring motivation, relationships and the darker psychological aspects of the story.
The atmosphere of the production was enhanced enormously by the professional theatre environment. Lighting, sound, staging, costumes and media were used to create the distinctive and atmospheric world of Victorian London.
For pupils involved, the production was an opportunity to experience a much more advanced level of musical theatre, requiring commitment, discipline, independent preparation and a high degree of collaboration.
With pupils from Years 9–13 working together, the production also provided an excellent opportunity for older pupils to develop leadership skills and for younger members of the cast to learn from more experienced performers.
Alongside our large-scale productions, LAMDA (London Academy of Music & Dramatic Art) tuition is offered throughout the school.
LAMDA provides pupils with the opportunity to develop their skills in speech and drama, acting, communication and musical theatre singing, with pupils working towards recognised examinations.
Pupils are encouraged to develop a strong understanding of voice, diction, articulation, projection, expression, characterisation and interpretation. They learn how to communicate meaningfully with an audience and how to use their voice and physical presence effectively.
LAMDA is particularly valuable because the skills developed extend far beyond the stage. Pupils become more confident speakers and communicators and develop the ability to present themselves clearly and confidently in front of others.
Across the school, multiple pupils undertake LAMDA examinations in Speech and Drama and Musical Theatre Singing, allowing them to work towards individual goals and receive recognition for their progress.
For some pupils, LAMDA becomes a pathway towards further study and performance; for others, it simply provides a supportive environment in which they can build confidence, overcome nerves and discover their own voice.
Our performing arts programme also gives pupils valuable experience of the many different aspects of putting on a professional production.
The Young Enterprise programme has played an important role in supporting the wider production experience. Pupils have been involved in selling tickets and developing products and refreshments for audiences to purchase during the interval.
This gives pupils the opportunity to see the commercial and organisational side of the performing arts industry. They develop practical skills in enterprise, marketing, customer service, budgeting, communication and sales, while contributing directly to the success of a major school production.
The experience reinforces an important message: a successful theatre production is not simply about what happens on stage. There is an entire organisation working behind the scenes to create the audience experience.
A Culture of Performance
Together, our productions, theatre opportunities and LAMDA programme create a strong culture of performance throughout Clayesmore.
Pupils are encouraged not only to perform but to understand the complete creative process. They experience the excitement of standing in the spotlight, the discipline of rehearsal, the responsibility of working as part of a cast, and the satisfaction of contributing to something much larger than themselves.
Whether performing in a large-scale musical, singing in an ensemble, acting in a dramatic production, working backstage, operating technical equipment, selling tickets through Young Enterprise or preparing for a LAMDA examination, pupils are given opportunities to find their voice, develop their confidence and discover their creativity.
The result is a performing arts programme that is inclusive, ambitious and genuinely exciting, providing pupils with experiences and memories that stay with them long after the final curtain.

pageCache.pageTitle: Clayesmore House Music 2026 | Prep and Senior Highlights
pageCache.text:
House Music 2026
This week, we closed the half term with two fantastic House Music Competitions across the Senior and Prep School.
Prep School
The Prep School came together for a toe-tapping House Music competition, with a fantastic Western theme bringing plenty of energy, laughter and musical talent to the stage!
Each house embraced the country spirit with their own brilliant performance. Seddons got everyone moving with 9 to 5, Edward-Stuarts took us down Country Roads, Rosses performed Jolene, and Everetts entertained the audience with The Gambler.
The fun didn’t stop with the pupils! Parents were invited to join in with a lively rendition of She’ll Be Coming Round the Mountain, before the whole school brought the event to a spectacular close with a singalong to Beyoncé’s TEXAS HOLD ’EM.
After an afternoon full of enthusiasm, teamwork and toe-tapping tunes, Everetts were crowned the winners! Congratulations to all four houses for making it such a memorable celebration of music and house spirit. Yeehaw!
Senior School
The school came together for a truly memorable House Music competition, filled with incredible performances, infectious energy and moments that will stay with us for a long time. From powerful ensemble performances to moving solo pieces, every house brought something special to the stage, making it a fantastic celebration of music and teamwork.
One of the standout highlights was Jonny’s energetic conducting, which captured the spirit of the competition and helped Gate secure the award for Best Conductor. The audience was also treated to a series of poignant and expressive solo performances from Zara, Luc, Logan and Eleni, each showcasing their individuality and musical talent. Zara’s outstanding performance earned Kings the award for Best Solo.
The ensemble performances were equally impressive, taking the audience on a musical journey from Jerusalem to the Arctic Monkeys and ABBA. Each house brought its own personality and style to the stage, creating an exciting mix of sounds and genres. Manor’s electric Arctic Monkeys ensemble particularly impressed the judges, winning Best Ensemble.
Of course, no House Music competition would be complete without the four fantastic unison pieces! Each house delivered a memorable performance:
The unison performances were a brilliant demonstration of teamwork, coordination and house pride. Wolverton’s performance of Love Me Like You stood out, earning them the award for Best Unison.
But it wasn’t all about being the centre of attention, and several students came together to accompany their peers’ unisons and ensemble pieces. Shining out was Eleni, who took Best Accompanist.
With their fantastic unison performance and an impressive contribution to the competition, Wolverton were crowned the overall winners! Their success was a wonderful end to an event that celebrated not only musical ability but also collaboration, confidence and the power of performing together.
Congratulations to Wolverton on their well-deserved victory, and a huge well done to every student who performed, composed, rehearsed and supported their house. House Music was a brilliant reminder that music brings people together, creates lasting memories and gives everyone a chance to shine.
What a performance, what a competition, and what a fantastic celebration of music across the school!
Kings: Can’t Stop This Feeling
Gate: Right Back Where We Started
Manor: Candy
Wolverton: Love Me Like You

Boarding Experience
Boarding at Clayesmore Prep is seriously fun!
Boarding life at Clayesmore Prep School closely resembles the atmosphere and diversity of a busy, loving and happy family, but with the advantage of being surrounded by friends 24 hours a day!
Around 50 girls and boys board with us in Aubrey House and are cared for by devoted Houseparents, Jess Chisholm and Tom Brown, with a team of matrons, nursing staff and tutors, whose focus is to provide a home-from-home environment.
Evenings are spent playing games, swimming, karaoke competitions, baking brownies, watching films, or enjoying barbecues. The children also get to relax and spend time with friends, just like at home. Mobile phone use (if students have access) is carefully monitored to allow calls home at specific times, but not much more.
Sundays are for expeditions, and the children head off to exciting new places every week, such as the coast for beach games, the Haynes Motor Museum, Dorset Water Park, Snowtrax, Monkey World and many other exciting locations.
A Home Away from Home
At Clayesmore, boarding isn’t just about where you sleep—it’s about belonging. We provide a warm, family-style environment where pupils feel supported, safe and empowered to grow. Our boarding culture is built around friendship, independence, and personal development. Pupils are surrounded by trusted adults who care deeply about their welfare and success, and who create a true home away from home.
Types of Boarding
At Clayesmore, we understand that every family’s circumstances are different, which is why we offer a flexible range of boarding options to suit individual needs and lifestyles.
Full Boarding
For pupils staying seven days a week throughout term time, full boarding offers the most immersive Clayesmore experience. Pupils become deeply involved in every aspect of school life—academic, pastoral, co-curricular and social. With structured weekends filled with enriching activities, trips, and time to unwind with friends, full boarders develop strong friendships and a powerful sense of belonging. It’s a wonderful environment for pupils to grow in independence, build resilience, and gain confidence in a secure, supportive setting.
Weekly Boarding
Weekly boarders stay from Monday to Saturday and return home after the end of commitments on Saturdays. This option is ideal for families living within a couple of hours’ drive of the school who want their children to enjoy the structure, community and enrichment of the boarding environment during the school week, while still spending some time at home. Weekly boarding offers the best of both worlds—academic focus and weekday independence, with regular family time.
Flexi Boarding
Flexi boarding offers the ultimate flexibility for modern family life. Pupils can board on specific nights when needed—whether due to long commutes, parental work commitments, school events, or as an introduction to boarding life. This option is perfect for pupils who want to take part in early or late activities, gain a little extra independence, or gradually ease into full-time boarding. Flexi boarders are fully integrated into house life during their stay and benefit from the same warm, supportive environment.
Exeats
Every half term, the school has one exeat weekend. On this weekend, most students will go home after school on Friday and return on Sunday evening. However, international students are able to stay at school for a weekend with a difference. Activities and trips are planned which showcase areas of the UK you may not yet have visited – a trip to London to watch a sports fixture, for example, or a trip to the theatre. The weekend brings our international community closer together and it is valued by the students.
Our Senior Boarding Houses
Clayesmore has six boarding houses—one for prep, two for boys and two for girls—each with its own personality and strong sense of community.
Each house is led by experienced Houseparents, supported by pastoral and academic staff who know every pupil personally.
Learn more about our Senior Boarding Houses
Benefits of Boarding
Boarding at Clayesmore helps pupils:
A Day in the Life
Morning: Wake up in cosy dorms, enjoy a hearty breakfast, and attend morning lessons.
Afternoon: Lunch and afternoon lessons or co-curricular activities.
Evening: Return to House, dinner with peers, prep (supervised study), and relaxing time in common rooms.
Saturday: LEX (Learning Enrichment and Extension) and sports fixtures.
Sunday: Trips, social events, and downtime to rest and prepare.
Exeats: International pupils may remain in school for a weekend of trips and organised activities whilst UK based students return home.

Support Every Step of the Way
Our dedicated boarding staff, Houseparents and Health and Wellbeing team work in unison to provide exceptional pastoral care. Whether pupils need help navigating teenage years, academic guidance, or health support, someone is always on hand. Boarders are never alone on their journey and are actively supported to flourish, both personally and academically.

pageCache.pageTitle: Music | Beyond the Classroom at Clayesmore
pageCache.text:
Music at Clayesmore
Music is a vibrant part of life at Clayesmore, giving every pupil the opportunity to sing, play, create and perform. From the earliest years, pupils develop their musicality through practical, engaging lessons, exploring a wide range of instruments, musical traditions and styles while building confidence, creativity and a lifelong love of music.
As pupils progress through the Prep and Senior Schools, opportunities continue to grow. Individual lessons with specialist teachers sit alongside a diverse programme of choirs, orchestras, bands and ensembles, including Chapel Choir, Concert Band, Orchestra, Jazz and Pop Bands, Chamber Strings, Pipe Band and Choral Society. There are regular concerts, recitals, performances and musical events throughout the year, giving musicians of every level the chance to perform, collaborate and develop their skills.
Music at Clayesmore Prep School
Sing. Play. Create. Perform. Belong.
Music is everywhere at Clayesmore Prep. It fills our classrooms, inspires our productions and brings our community together. Our dynamic music programme gives every child the opportunity to discover their musical voice while developing confidence, creativity and a lifelong love of music.
Every pupil from Years 1–8 has a dedicated weekly music lesson with our Director of Music (Prep), Charlotte McCarthy (BMus, MMus). In our specialist music classroom, pupils learn through singing, playing, composing, listening and performing, with music theory naturally woven into practical music-making.
From the earliest years, lessons are energetic and hands-on. Pre-Prep pupils explore rhythm, movement, songs and Dalcroze Eurhythmics, while older pupils develop their musicianship through an increasingly diverse programme of musical styles and traditions.
From Western classical music to jazz, blues, reggae, gamelan, steel pans, musical theatre, film music and contemporary music, pupils discover how music can connect them to different cultures and ideas.
Our music room is equipped with an exciting range of instruments, including drums, steel pans, ukuleles, keyboards, recorders, xylophones, percussion and orchestral instruments, giving pupils the opportunity to experiment and make music together.
Music continues beyond the classroom through a thriving programme of choirs, ensembles and performances. Pupils can join Junior, Senior and Chamber Choirs, recorder and ukulele groups, steel pans, African drumming, rock bands and other instrumental groups. Music also plays an important role in weekly Chapel services.
Performance is central to the Clayesmore experience. Pupils take part in lunchtime concerts, whole-school concerts, community performances and special celebrations, while our annual productions give them the opportunity to develop their confidence on a larger stage. Years 6–8 perform a major musical production in the Clayesmore Theatre each spring.
Individual instrumental and vocal lessons are also available with our team of specialist visiting teachers, with pupils encouraged to celebrate their progress through ABRSM, Trinity College London and Rockschool examinations.
At Clayesmore Prep, every child has the opportunity to discover the excitement of making music, develop their confidence and creativity, and find their place within a thriving musical community.
Music at Clayesmore Senior School
Music is a vibrant part of life at Clayesmore Senior School, with opportunities for musicians of every level to develop their skills, perform and discover new musical interests. Based in our purpose-built Music School, the department is led by two full-time teachers alongside a dedicated team of specialist visiting teachers.
Pupils can take part in an extensive programme of choirs, ensembles and bands, including Chapel Choir, Orchestra, Concert Band, Choral Society, Chamber Strings, Jazz Band, Pop Bands, Brass Ensemble and Pipe Band. There are also opportunities for smaller groups and individual musicians to perform, ensuring that pupils can find an ensemble suited to their interests and experience.
Performance is at the heart of the department, with a busy programme of concerts and events throughout the year. Highlights include the Festive Extravaganza, Charity Showcase Concert, summer ‘Hampers and Champers’ concert, House Music Competition, Open Mic Nights, chamber concerts, Piano Club recitals and May Morning Madrigals. Musicians regularly perform both individually and as part of larger ensembles.
Chapel Choir plays an important role in school life, leading Friday Chapel services and performing at major events including Remembrance and Carol Services. The choir also performs beyond the school, while the Choral Society brings together pupils, staff and parents to perform major works.
For advanced musicians, there are opportunities to take part in county and national ensembles, specialist music courses and external performance opportunities. Music Scholarships are available in Year 9 and the Sixth Form.
Music can also be pursued academically through GCSE, A-level Music and Music Technology BTEC, with pupils achieving strong results and developing their skills as performers, composers and informed listeners.
Whether performing in an ensemble, taking to the stage as a soloist or pursuing music academically, Clayesmore gives pupils the opportunity to develop their musical ability, confidence and creativity.
For those who wish to pursue music further, GCSE, A-level Music and Music Technology provide opportunities for more advanced academic study, while Music Scholarships recognise exceptional talent and commitment. Pupils are also encouraged to take part in county and national music groups, courses and competitions beyond school.
Whether discovering music for the first time or performing demanding repertoire, every Clayesmorian can find their place in our musical community and develop the confidence, creativity and discipline that music inspires.

pageCache.pageTitle: Learning Support for Dyslexia and ADHD | Clayesmore School
pageCache.text:
Learning Support
High academic achievement begins with a deep professional commitment to understanding how children learn.
For more than 25 years, the school has been recognised nationally for its expertise in supporting pupils with dyslexia, dyspraxia, ADHD and other learning differences, and we are proud to hold CReSTeD accreditation. However, what distinguishes Clayesmore is that this expertise shapes teaching and learning across the entire school.
Our work is led by the Deputy Head Academic and the SENCO, supported by a specialist team able to assess pupils carefully and provide detailed guidance for teachers. All teaching and pastoral staff are trained not simply in what children need to learn, but in how children learn effectively. This influences lesson design, classroom routines, revision strategies and approaches to feedback across every subject.
Teachers use explicit instruction, carefully sequenced learning, retrieval practice, collaborative discussion and visual explanation to help pupils develop confidence and independence. The approaches which best support pupils with dyslexia, slower processing or concentration difficulties almost always are the same approaches that improve learning for everyone.
This understanding also shapes the school’s wider expectations and routines. We believe strongly in high standards, while recognising that memory, organisation, executive functioning and attention are skills which need to be taught and reinforced. Expectations remain high, but our responses are always thoughtful, proportionate and educational.
This approach enables a wide range of pupils to succeed. Recent leavers have progressed to Oxford to study Mathematics and English, while former pupils have gone on to complete doctorates at, among many other places, Warwick, Cambridge and Imperial College London.

pageCache.pageTitle: Inspired Learning Group | Clayesmore School Partnership
pageCache.text:
Inspired Learning Group
We Are Part Of Inspired Learning Group
Clayesmore School is proud to be part of the Inspired Learning Group (ILG), a growing family of independent schools and nurseries across the UK. ILG is committed to supporting each school in achieving excellence while preserving its unique character, heritage, and values.
Our Aim
At ILG, we strive to create safe, inspiring, and ambitious learning environments where young people can flourish academically, socially, and personally. We believe education should equip pupils not only with knowledge and skills, but also with the confidence, resilience, and character needed to make a positive contribution to society and embrace the opportunities of a rapidly changing world.
Through a combination of traditional values and innovative thinking, ILG schools empower every pupil to realise their full potential and prepare for futures that are continually evolving.
Our Philosophy
At the heart of ILG’s philosophy is a commitment to putting every child first. We believe that educational excellence is achieved through a culture of care, where pupils feel valued, supported, and encouraged to be the very best version of themselves.
At Clayesmore, this means providing a broad and enriching educational experience that extends beyond the classroom. Alongside academic achievement, we place great importance on co-curricular opportunities, personal development, leadership, and wellbeing, ensuring our pupils leave school as confident, compassionate, and capable young adults ready to thrive in the twenty-first century.
ILG Founder – Amit Mehta
Amit Mehta began his career with Fortune 500 company Avery Dennison, where he rapidly progressed into senior leadership, reporting directly to the Chief Financial Officer. During his ten years with the organisation, he developed a deep understanding of what drives successful businesses and high-performing teams.
He later built and expanded two private equity-backed businesses, gaining extensive experience in leadership, customer engagement, and organisational growth. As his own family grew, Amit sought an opportunity that combined commercial success with meaningful social impact. This led him to acquire and transform a group of struggling schools, helping secure their futures and preserving valuable educational opportunities for local communities.
Recognising the profound difference that excellent education can make, Amit founded the Inspired Learning Group in 2014. Since then, ILG has grown significantly, bringing together a diverse portfolio of independent schools and nurseries while maintaining a clear focus on educational quality, pupil wellbeing, and community engagement.
Today, Amit remains passionate about applying his business expertise to education. He works closely with school leaders, teachers, parents, and pupils to enhance educational outcomes, strengthen communities, and create environments where young people can thrive.

pageCache.text:
Curriculum
Our Curriculum
Our Pre-Prep curriculum provides a strong foundation for every child’s educational journey, combining academic excellence with creativity, curiosity and a love of learning.
In Reception, learning follows the Early Years Foundation Stage, where children continue their development through play, exploration and carefully planned experiences. As they move into Years 1 and 2, they begin the Key Stage 1 curriculum, building secure foundations in phonics, reading, writing, mathematics and science. Alongside these core subjects, children explore history, geography, art, design and technology, computing, music, PE and PSHE through engaging, hands-on learning.
We believe children learn best when they are actively involved in their education. Specialist teaching, outdoor learning, Forest School, educational visits and enrichment activities are woven throughout the curriculum, helping pupils make meaningful connections and discover new passions.
Above all, our curriculum is designed to develop confident, curious and compassionate learners. We encourage children to ask questions, solve problems, think independently and work collaboratively, equipping them with the skills, knowledge and confidence to flourish throughout their time at Clayesmore and beyond.

pageCache.pageTitle: Prep School Curriculum | Years 3–8 at Clayesmore Dorset
pageCache.text:
Prep Curriculum
Curriculum Overviews
At Clayesmore Prep School, our curriculum is carefully designed to inspire curiosity, challenge pupils academically and support every stage of their development. As children progress through the school, learning evolves from a nurturing, class-based environment to a more specialist and independent approach, preparing them confidently for senior school and beyond.
Across all year groups, pupils benefit from a broad and balanced curriculum that combines strong academic foundations with creative, practical and experiential learning opportunities. Specialist teaching, outdoor education, enrichment activities and the values of the Clayesmore Compass help pupils develop the knowledge, skills and personal qualities needed to thrive both inside and outside the classroom.
Explore each stage of the Prep School curriculum below to discover how learning develops from Years 3 and 4 through to Year 8.
In Years 3, 4, and 5 children begin their journey through the Prep School with a broad, engaging curriculum designed to build strong foundations in key skills while nurturing curiosity and confidence.
Learning is delivered primarily by a class teacher, ensuring consistency, strong relationships and close pastoral care. As a result, children feel secure and supported as they develop independence and a love of learning.
The curriculum focuses on core skills in English and Mathematics, alongside Science, Humanities, Languages, Creative Arts, Computing, PE and Outdoor Education. Lessons are practical, creative and interactive, encouraging children to explore ideas, ask questions and make connections across subjects.
As well as developing academic skills, pupils begin to build independence through structured prep and are introduced to specialist teaching in areas such as music, PE, computing and languages. Outdoor learning, trips and enrichment activities bring learning to life and help children develop confidence beyond the classroom.
At the heart of learning is the Clayesmore Compass — Communication, Consideration, Creativity and Courage — which helps pupils develop positive attitudes and strong personal foundations for future success.
In Year 6, pupils move into a more specialist teaching model while continuing to benefit from strong pastoral support through their tutor and form system.
This stage marks an important transition as pupils become more independent learners, developing confidence, responsibility and deeper academic understanding across all subjects.
The curriculum builds on strong foundations in English and Mathematics, while introducing greater depth and challenge in Science, Humanities, Languages, Computing and the Creative Arts. Pupils are encouraged to think more critically, work collaboratively and take greater ownership of their learning.
Specialist teaching becomes more frequent, and pupils benefit from a wide range of enrichment opportunities including outdoor education, fieldwork, performances and residential experiences.
Prep becomes a more structured part of learning, helping pupils develop organisation, time management and independent study skills.
The Clayesmore Compass continues to underpin all aspects of school life, supporting pupils in developing communication, creativity, courage and consideration as they prepare for the next stage of their education.
In Year 7, pupils enter Key Stage 3 learning while still within the supportive environment of the Prep School, ensuring a smooth and confident transition towards senior school education.
All subjects are taught by specialist teachers, allowing pupils to explore greater depth and complexity across the curriculum. Learning becomes more analytical and independent, with a strong focus on developing critical thinking, problem-solving and subject-specific skills.
The curriculum includes English, Mathematics, Science, Humanities, Languages, Computing, Creative Arts, PE and PSHRE, with increased emphasis on applying knowledge in more challenging and extended tasks.
Pupils are encouraged to take greater responsibility for their learning, manage their workload effectively and develop resilience and independence in preparation for future academic demands.
Enrichment continues through trips, performances, outdoor learning and leadership opportunities, helping pupils to broaden their experiences and build confidence.
In Year 8, pupils reach the final year of Prep School and are fully prepared for transition into senior school and GCSE study.
The curriculum is challenging, broad and academically ambitious, delivered by specialist teachers who encourage independence, depth of understanding and strong analytical thinking.
Pupils study a wide range of subjects including English, Mathematics, Science, Humanities, Languages, Computing, Creative Arts, PE and PSHRE. Learning focuses on applying knowledge, developing advanced skills and preparing for the expectations of senior school study.
There is a strong emphasis on independent learning, organisation and personal responsibility. Pupils are encouraged to think critically, reflect on their progress and take ownership of their academic development.
Enrichment plays an important role in Year 8, with leadership opportunities, trips, performances and outdoor experiences helping pupils build confidence and maturity.
By the end of Year 8, pupils leave Clayesmore Prep as confident, capable and well-rounded individuals, fully prepared for the next stage of their education.

pageCache.pageTitle: Senior School Curriculum | GCSE Options at Clayesmore Dorset
pageCache.text:
Senior Curriculum
YEAR 9 – YEAR 11
In Year 9 students study English, Mathematics, Biology, Chemistry, Physics, Geography, History, IT, Food and Nutrition, Design Technology, Art and PE. Each week Year 9s also have lessons, taught by senior staff, in debating, presentation skills, conservation and critical thinking. If it is appropriate they will study both French and Spanish. They all play sport three times a week – on Mondays, Thursdays and Saturdays. On Saturdays they have LEX sessions, more details of which can be found here.
In March – April of Year 9 students choose their GCSE Options. Everyone takes English Language, Maths and Science. Most also take English Literature and some also take Further Mathematics.
Students then choose up to 4 additional optional subjects, leading to between 6 and 11 GCSEs.
The optional subjects are: Art and Design, Computer Science, Creative iMedia, Design and Technology, Food Preparation and Nutrition, French, Spanish, Geography, History, Music, PE.
Students who have some learning support usually have their support lessons in place of one or sometimes two optional subjects. This is discussed in detail with parents and pupils.
Science: more able scientists take three separate sciences. Students who find Science less interesting or useful have lessons in all three sciences and take the combined science award.
International students can be prepared for a globally recognised IGCSE in English as a Second Language. Some international students also take a GCSE in their own language if it is offered by the exam board. We have recently had students take a qualification in German, French, Italian, Greek, Mandarin, Japanese and Turkish.

pageCache.text:
Sixth Form Curriculum
Years 12–13 Curriculum Overview
Students take three subjects made up of A Levels and/or BTECs.
A Levels are offered in Art, Design Technology / Product Design, Music, Photography, English Literature, French, Spanish, Maths, Physics, Chemistry, Biology, Economics, Business, Geography, History, Psychology. And BTECs in Enterprise and Entrepreneurship, Sport, Creative Digital Media and Music Technology.
BTECs are vocational subjects strongly related to work. They are assessed, usually, via 2 exams and 2 coursework modules. Students do very well in them.
Students may also do an Extended Project Qualification if they would like to do so, which is worth half an A Level but which universities value very highly. Those wishing to apply for Art School, Medical School or to Oxbridge are encouraged to do so and supported in their preparation for these applications.
During the timetabled week, all Year 12s also undertake some community service with local projects and have careers lessons and lessons to help them navigate the university entrance process. On Saturday mornings, students pursue a wide range of activities, some of which are related to their academic work, and further information about these can be found here.

pageCache.text:
Fee Support / Bursaries
Fee Support and Bursaries
At Clayesmore, we believe that a child’s education should be shaped by their potential, not limited by financial circumstances. We are committed to making a Clayesmore education accessible to bright, curious and enthusiastic children through a range of means-tested fee support options.
Financial assistance is available through means-tested bursaries. Families wishing to apply are invited to complete a bursary application form, which is reviewed confidentially by the School’s Bursary Committee. Bursary awards are tailored to each family’s individual circumstances and are intended to help make a Clayesmore education more accessible. The level of support available varies from case to case and is subject to both financial assessment and the School’s bursary budget. While bursaries can make a significant contribution towards school fees, they are generally intended to provide assistance with the cost of a Clayesmore education rather than full fee remission. Although we endeavour to support as many families as possible, bursary awards cannot be guaranteed in every case.
Sibling Discount
The School offers a 5% fee discount for the eldest sibling on roll and a 10% discount for each subsequent sibling attending the School concurrently. Our Admissions team is always happy to discuss the fee support options available and guide families through the application process.

Immersion Groups
British Boarding School Experience
The Inspired Learning Group offers a British Boarding School Experience across its schools, including Clayesmore School, Shebbear College, Saint Felix School, and St Francis College (girls only), for students aged 10–18.
Our programmes are carefully designed for international students to experience life in a British boarding school. Students are fully integrated into the daily routines at Clayesmore School, providing a genuine insight into school life in the UK. This includes attending lessons, participating in co-curricular activities, and engaging in the wider school community.
Alongside academic learning, students develop their English language skills through real-life interaction, improving their speaking, listening, reading, and writing in a natural and supportive environment. Cultural activities further enrich the experience, helping students gain a deeper understanding of British traditions and lifestyle.
This experience builds confidence, strengthens communication skills, and supports a smooth transition into UK education. It also provides an excellent opportunity for students to form lasting friendships with peers from around the world, broadening their global perspective.
Programmes can run from one week to several weeks and are available for individual families, visiting school groups, and educational agents. As well as being a rewarding experience, this programme offers an ideal introduction for students considering full-time study at one of our schools.
Please click on the links to explore our schools further, or email Cllewellyn@clayesmore.com for advice, availability, and bookings.
